focus.label: Acute epididymo-orchitis
focus.why: node-4 purulent foci/enlarged epididymis/infected appendages => infection; node-3 occult penis predisposes; node-2 no LUTS favors scrotal infection.

payload.query: Need scrotal ultrasound and laboratory inflammatory markers (e.g., WBC, CRP) to confirm acute epididymo-orchitis and assess for abscess or alternative pathology.

Need the surgical exploration findings or emergency urology consultation record, because follow-up sonography revealed a mild whirlpool sign and inguinal hyperechogenicity, which may indicate spermatic cord torsion despite the purulent infection; this is critical to definitively confirm acute epididymo-orchitis and exclude a surgical emergency.

payload.analysis: Believing acute epididymo-orchitis, lab tests show leukocytosis and P. aeruginosa growth, confirming infection; Doppler ultrasound shows enlarged testis with preserved blood flow, refuting torsion, despite a mild whirlpool sign on follow-up. Absent surgical exploration, the infectious findings and negative urinalysis strongly support scrotal infection. All key retrievable information is covered; urgent urology review is advised.

payload.query: Need scrotal Doppler ultrasound to confirm hyperemia and assess abscess formation, along with laboratory tests (blood WBC, CRP, urinalysis) to substantiate acute infection and definitively exclude torsion or tumor.

Need scrotal Doppler ultrasound to confirm hyperemia and assess abscess formation, along with laboratory tests (blood WBC, CRP, urinalysis) to substantiate acute infection and definitively exclude torsion or tumor.

Need serum tumor markers (AFP, hCG) and CRP to complete the infectious workup and definitively exclude testicular tumor, as the heterogeneous echo pattern on Doppler can mimic malignancy; also need contrast-enhanced scrotal ultrasound or MRI to assess for abscess formation and guide management.
